about: Verdict vectors: for each case, the acts a verifier holds (by id, from the pool: each act's complete bytes, outside, locked inside and signature, as Envelopes encodes an act; every act public, its content key on its outside), the facts it holds beside them that are not acts (inclusion proofs a home served, each naming the receipt it proves; homes it failed to reach; anchors it checked; rail answers it was given: that a receipt or claim is valid, paid to a flow, and which payment a proof is; the specifications of rail Modules it adopted, whose fields 11 and 13 give each rail's kind and what its proof binds; receipts and claims a rail answered invalid; a private act's content key, as its recipient holds it; private acts found at a home, with the home's operator; a judge's period passed on a question, and settlements signed before their link's stage opened, as the time reference says), the question asked and the verdict the texts give, with the rule that decides it. Questions: status (Identity's standing of an act: valid, pending, void, disputed, invalid, unknown, scoped, not counting); chain (the acts counting at each position of an identity chain, what stops it, and homes proven dishonest from a position on); succession (Identity, "Succession": none, declared, confirmed and followed, unknown, or another protocol's, with the successor and its confirmation); status after keepers (Identity's standing once Agreements has read the keeper records held and named the acts their keepers recorded before the rotation voiding them); backing (Agreements rule 80 for an act of a grant key); consent counts (whether an act for a collective has the consent its layer's rule, or the finer area reaching it, needs); agreement exists; deal fork; deadline (rule 33, under the keepers and rule given, on the clock given, at the point given); closing and fork (whether a collective's closing or fork is complete); version in force (a deal's, as its chain of judgment settles it); vow (each sale's state, the payments signed by nobody, and those whose place is unknown); purchase contests (the contests shown beside a purchase, by the act that is it: the buyer's payer's claim of the payment, or the buyer's signature act on an offer at no price; or unknown); refund repaid (what Money shows paid back toward a refund, or unknown); paid toward (what counts toward an obligation, or unknown where it rests on a payment the rail's answer does not name); payment counts (whether a receipt or claim the rail answered paid counts for its payee, Money rules 4 and 12 to 15: counts, does not count, or unknown); purchase (Agreements rule 12's verdict on a receipt or claim: purchase, no purchase, unrecorded, wrong receipt, unknown, or not a payment for a work); disagreements (how many open questions a receiver shows, Money rule 11, or unknown likewise); specification claim (Development rule 3: whether a publication claims a specification for the creator given: claimed, unclaimed, unclaimed shown as disputed, or unknown); agreement invalid (whether an agreement's terms are invalid, a false mark included, or refused outside their format: invalid, not invalid, or unknown); liveness (whether a party's liveness act shows presence: shows presence, shows nothing, or unknown); price tag (Money rule 18, as a verifier reading Money and Envelopes tells it: counts, nobody's offer, or unknown, a tag under a publication being Agreements' to judge); transfer (Agreements rule 10: whether a stake transfer takes effect, and the seller's payout receipts after its place on the seller's own line, wrong receipts); split (rules 15 and 30: the holders and partners a split pays other than its plan says, any breaking the plan); record (rule 69: whether a record of the collective given is a line, and the clone it puts in force, or null); owed back by (rule 11: who owes a payment racing an ending back, and how much: the split service from what it holds, then each party in the share it received); work owners (Agreements rule 15, "Claim (type 3)": the claims that count and bind a work, and its default holder); route to and route from (Money rules 24 to 28: the route ending at a receipt or claim, as its final creditor reads it, or starting at a receipt, followed forward: valid with its records, stopped at the receipt whose forward is not carried on with that open obligation, broken at a record with the agreement the failure names, or unknown). The MIR hashes are stand-ins, SHA-256 of a label, until the freeze: identity, envelopes, text, money, agreements, development below. Every key is test data derived from a name.

agreements.name: a deal one party has not signed: does not exist
agreements.why: A deal exists once every party has signed it.

agreements.name: a deal every party signed: exists
agreements.why: Terms plus every party's signature act.

agreements.name: two complete versions of one version: a fork, the version before it the reference
agreements.why: Every party signed both; neither is in force; the reference stays.

agreements.name: a collective's act its layer's rule needs two members for, signed by one: does not count
agreements.why: The rule for Money is [2, [ana, ben]]: Cy drafts the pointer, with his own key, naming the collective; Ana alone signs it.

agreements.name: the same signed by both members it names: counts
agreements.why: Ana's and Ben's signature acts name it.

agreements.name: an act of a grant key within its reach, the grant accepted: backed
agreements.why: A person's grant reaching publications.

agreements.name: an act the revocation's history holds: binds
agreements.why: It is in the revocation's history (the revocation cites it).

agreements.name: an act the revocation misses, nobody else acknowledging it: void
agreements.why: Racing the revocation, relied on by nobody.

agreements.name: an act the revocation misses, another identity acknowledging it: disputed
agreements.why: A fan acknowledged it by a witness act: valid, shown disputed, conferring nothing unless the grantor adopts it.

agreements.name: an act the revocation misses, only its grantee acknowledging it: void
agreements.why: The grantee's own acknowledgement does not count.

agreements.name: an act the revocation misses, recorded by a keeper of a deal it belongs to before the revocation: disputed
agreements.why: It names the deal in objects; the deal's keeper recorded it, then the revocation.

agreements.name: a deal's keeper recorded the act before the rotation: disputed
agreements.why: Only a record before the keeper's own record of the rotation, in its sequence, counts against it.

agreements.name: the deal's keeper recorded the act only after the rotation: void
agreements.why: Only a record before the keeper's own record of the rotation, in its sequence, counts against it.

agreements.name: a keeper's record of an act belonging to its deal at depth two, before the rotation: disputed
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Belongs to" (no fixed depth); rules 41 and 42; Identity rule 34
agreements.why: The receipt fulfils an obligation, and the obligation arises from the deal (its field 4): the receipt belongs to the deal, whose keeper recorded it before recording the rotation.

agreements.name: the same at a verifier not holding the obligation: unknown
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Belongs to": unknown beyond an act not held; Identity, "A verifier that cannot tell answers unknown"
agreements.why: Whether the receipt belongs to an agreement whose keepers recorded it lies beyond the obligation, which is not held: void cannot be told.

agreements.name: a party's contest naming an obligation of the deal in objects, recorded by the deal's keeper before the rotation: disputed
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Belongs to" (each objects entry one step, whatever the act named is); rules 41, 42 and 54; Identity rule 34
agreements.why: The contest names the obligation as chain and predecessor; the obligation arises from the deal (its field 4). Each objects entry is one step, whatever the act it names, so the contest belongs to the deal, and the keeper the deal names recorded it before recording the rotation.

agreements.name: an act naming the founding, its history holding a clone in force: the clone's keeper recorded it before the rotation: disputed
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Belongs to": its keepers are those of the version in force for the act; rules 41 and 42
agreements.why: The act names the founding; its history (its prev, Ana's signature of the clone) holds the clone, complete: the version in force for it is the clone, whose keepers alone speak for it.

agreements.name: the same recorded only by the founding's keeper, whom the clone replaced: void
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Belongs to": its keepers are those of the version in force for the act; rules 41 and 42
agreements.why: The act names the founding; its history (its prev, Ana's signature of the clone) holds the clone, complete: the version in force for it is the clone, whose keepers alone speak for it.

agreements.name: a collective's act of the payment cMIP an operational clone names, after the record putting that clone in force: counts
agreements.rule: Agreements, record (type 17): an operational clone recorded is in force at once; rules 60 and 65
agreements.why: The founding names one payment cMIP for task 6; the clone, marked by the power of the rule for Money, names another; Cy records it for the collective, and its next act, citing the record, of that cMIP, falls in Money and has Ben's signature, whom the rule for Money names.

agreements.name: the same kind of act signed before the record: does not count
agreements.why: Before the record the founding is in force, which names that cMIP for no task: the act falls in no layer the agreement names a rule for.

agreements.name: a record naming the signatures that meet its clone's mark: the clone in force, a collective's act of the cMIP it names counts
agreements.why: The rule for Money names Ben and Cy, both; the clone is marked by that rule's power; the record names both their signatures, so the clone is complete at the record and in force from it.

agreements.name: a record naming valid signatures short of its clone's mark: the clone not in force
agreements.rule: Agreements, record (type 17): the clone complete at the record only if the signatures it names meet its mark; rule 65
agreements.why: The record names one of the two signatures the mark needs, though both signed: counted at the record, they fall short of the mark, so the clone is not put in force; the act of the cMIP it names falls in no layer of the founding.

agreements.name: a record naming a clone whose parent is not the agreement in force for it: the clone not in force
agreements.rule: Agreements, record (type 17): the clone's parent is the agreement in force for the record
agreements.why: A first record put a clone of the founding in force; a second record names another clone of the founding, complete, but its parent is no longer the agreement in force, so it is not put in force; the act of the cMIP it names falls in no layer of the clone in force.

agreements.name: a collective's closing signed by every member with a chain signature: complete
agreements.why: Every voice of the agreement in force signed it with its chain key; the collective owes nothing and holds no stake.

agreements.name: the same, one member's chain signature not held: not complete
agreements.why: A closing needs every voice: the third member's chain signature is not among the acts held.

agreements.name: an act of the collective after its closing: it does not count
agreements.why: Closed: what is signed for the collective afterwards counts for nothing, whoever the rule for Text names signing or not.

agreements.name: a closing of a collective owing a refund on a payment to it: not complete
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Closing (type 20)": the collective owes nothing, a refund owed on a payment to it among its debts
agreements.why: The fan paid the band naming another seller's tag: no purchase, money received for nothing, owed back to the fan. The refund is a debt of the band's, not ended: the band cannot close while it owes it.

agreements.name: the same, the fan's own receipt of the refund held: the closing complete
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Closing (type 20)": the collective owes nothing, a refund owed on a payment to it among its debts
agreements.why: The fan receipts 300 back, naming the payment refunded: the refund is repaid, and the band owes nothing.

agreements.name: an act of the collective before its closing: it still counts
agreements.why: What was signed for it before the closing, by the member the rule for Text names, stands.

agreements.name: a collective's closing signed by every remaining member after a registered resignation: complete
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 91; "Closing"; Resignation, registered by a record
agreements.why: Cy resigned, and the collective's record registered it, so Cy's voice is removed before the closing; Ana and Ben, every remaining voice, signed the closing with their chain keys.

agreements.name: a collective's closing under a constitutional rule counted by shares, signed by a member holding more than the share: complete
agreements.why: The constitutional rule is half of the stake's shares; Ana holds six tenths and signed the closing with her chain key: decided, whatever the others do.

agreements.name: a collective's fork into two sides, each successor founded first, signed by every member with a chain signature: complete
agreements.why: Every member on its sides signed it with its chain key, meeting the constitutional rule; each successor's founding names the original and fits its side; there is no debt to hand out.

agreements.name: the same, one member's chain signature not held: not complete
agreements.why: The constitutional rule is every party: the second member's chain signature is not among the acts held.

agreements.name: an act of the original after its fork: it does not count
agreements.why: The original is closed in Agreements by its fork: what its keys sign afterwards counts for nothing.

agreements.name: an act of the original before its fork: it still counts
agreements.why: What it signed before the fork, with its area's holder, stands.

agreements.name: a deal one of whose parties is an agreement, signed by the other party and by every party of that agreement: exists
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 1; an agreement as a party, named by its line
agreements.why: The inner agreement signs through its own parties, Ana and Ben; Cy signs for itself.

agreements.name: the same without one party of the inner agreement signing it: does not exist
agreements.why: Ben, a party of the agreement that is a party, has not signed: the inner agreement has not signed.

agreements.name: a deal one of whose parties is an agreement standing forked, unsettled, signed by the other party and by every party of the inner agreement's reference: exists
agreements.rule: Agreements rules 1, 46 and 47; an agreement as a party, its version in force signing
agreements.why: The inner deal has two complete versions of its founding, neither settled: by rule 47 the reference, the founding, stays in force, and its parties, Ana and Ben, sign for it.

agreements.name: a deal's fork settled by the judge its terms name, within its period: the version kept is in force
agreements.why: The judge of forks answers the settlement request, keeping A.

agreements.name: the next link of the chain settling while the first judge's period runs: the deal stays on its reference
agreements.why: Only the judge whose stage is open settles; the first judge's period has not passed.

agreements.name: the first judge's period passed with no answer: the next link settles, keeping B
agreements.why: The time reference says the first judge's period passed; the next link's settlement within its stage counts, its earlier one, signed before its stage opened, does not.

agreements.name: the first judge answering after its period: counts for nothing, the next link's settlement stands
agreements.why: A judge speaking after its period has passed has no say.

agreements.name: a judge's two first settlements keeping different versions: the next link active, its settlement in force
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 35; the chain of judgment
agreements.why: A judge that contradicts itself has answered unknown: the next link is active with no period to wait, and its settlement, keeping B, counts.

agreements.name: a judge's settlement naming every tip it saw: the version kept is in force
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 47, "What a settlement could see"; "The judge of forks"
agreements.why: The deal has three complete versions of its founding; the judge keeps A and names B and C as the tips it drops.

agreements.name: a judge's settlement omitting a tip it saw: it counts for nothing
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 47, "What a settlement could see": it counts only where it names every tip it saw
agreements.why: The version kept, A, cites version C, so A's history holds C and the judge's settlement saw C through the history of the version it keeps; it neither keeps nor names C: it settles nothing, and the deal stays on its reference.

agreements.name: a deadline met by an anchor of the act
agreements.verdict: met, by an anchor of the act
agreements.why: An anchor of the act at or before the point shows it made in time.

agreements.name: a deadline met by both keepers' records lying before their records anchored by the point
agreements.verdict: met, by the keepers' anchored records
agreements.why: Each keeper's record of the act lies before a record of its anchored at or before the point; the rule is all.

agreements.name: a deadline missed: both keepers' sequences anchored past the point hold no record of the act
agreements.why: Their records anchored at 150 have no record of the act before them.

agreements.name: a deadline with no anchor: undetermined
agreements.why: A keeper's sequence orders; only anchors place anything on the clock.

agreements.name: an anchor of the act wins over the keepers' silence
agreements.verdict: met, by an anchor of the act
agreements.why: The act is anchored at the point; the keepers' anchored sequences lack it.

agreements.name: a buyer's contest of their purchase: shown beside it
agreements.why: The fan's own payer's claim is the purchase; the fan signs a contest naming it, the promise not kept in words. It is shown beside the purchase and voids nothing.

agreements.name: the same contest signed by another identity: shows nothing
agreements.why: Only the buyer of a purchase has standing to contest it; signed by anyone else, the contest shows nothing.

agreements.name: a judge's settlement keeping A and dropping B, its request's history holding a third version C: it counts for nothing
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 47, "What a settlement could see": what it cites, each with its own history
agreements.why: The judge's settlement cites the request; the requester signed C before asking, so the request's history, and with it the settlement's, holds C. It neither keeps nor names C: it settles nothing, and the deal stays on its reference.

agreements.name: the same settlement naming C among the tips it drops: the version kept is in force
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 47, "What a settlement could see"
agreements.why: Every version of the fork the settlement saw, through the request's history and the versions' own, is on the line it keeps or a tip it names.

agreements.name: a sale of a collective's work under its publication, naming the collective's own ownership agreement: a purchase
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 12; the glossary, "Stake": a stake in the collective itself is a share of all its income
agreements.why: The publication is the collective's, naming its ownership agreement, selling its album; its split service prices it and records the payment, and the fan's claim names the agreement (field 9). The collective's stake in itself is a stake in every work it sells.

agreements.name: the fan's contest of that purchase: shown beside it
agreements.why: The sale is a purchase, so the buyer's own contest naming the claim is shown beside it.

agreements.name: a deal's fork settled by its parties: a complete version on one branch naming the other's tip, the version in force
agreements.why: A clone of A, naming B in field 26 and citing it after its parent, signed by both parties: from it on, its line is in force.

agreements.name: two settlements of the parties, neither holding the other, keeping different lines: tangled, on the reference
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 47, "Two settlements of one fork, neither holding the other"
agreements.why: Every party signed both settlements, each naming the other branch's tip; neither's history holds the other.

agreements.name: the parties' settlement against the judge's, neither holding the other: the parties' holds
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 47, "Two settlements of one fork, neither holding the other"
agreements.why: The judge keeps A; the parties, not citing the judge's settlement, settle on B. A version every party signed is the deal changing by its own rule; the judge's counts for nothing.

agreements.name: a settling version naming a tip this verifier does not hold: a plain version, the deal on its reference
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 47, "A settling version naming a version this verifier does not hold"
agreements.why: The verifier holds everything but B's newer version, which the settlement names: it reads the settlement as a plain version on A's branch until it holds it.

agreements.name: the same once the verifier holds the tip it names: the settlement counts
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 47, "A settling version naming a version this verifier does not hold"
agreements.why: From then on it counts as a settlement.

agreements.name: a deal with two keepers under the rule "every keeper", only one recording the act before the rotation: void
agreements.why: The first keeper recorded the act before the rotation, the second only after it; the keepers' rule decides whether that is enough.

agreements.name: the same under the rule "at least one keeper": disputed
agreements.why: The first keeper recorded the act before the rotation, the second only after it; the keepers' rule decides whether that is enough.

agreements.name: a payment naming a claimed work's bake, no price tag: a tip to its uploader, no payment for a work
agreements.rule: Money rule 18: a payment naming a bake without a tag is a tip to its uploader, no purchase; Agreements rule 12
agreements.verdict: not a payment for a work
agreements.why: The film is owned by Ana and Ben's ownership agreement and sold by their publication's price tag; Cy's payment names the bake itself, no tag: a tip to Ana, its uploader, neither a purchase nor money owed back.

agreements.name: the same payment naming the publication's price tag, the receipt naming the ownership agreement: a purchase
agreements.why: Ana, the publication's split service, receipts the payment of its tag; field 9 names the ownership agreement and its version.

agreements.name: a payment of a lone seller's price tag, naming no ownership agreement: a purchase
agreements.rule: Agreements rules 11 and 12: a lone seller's publication; its split service's receipt carries no field 9
agreements.why: The publication names no ownership agreement (field 1); the seller is its own split service, and its receipt of a payment of the tag carries no field 9: a purchase under the publication's terms.

agreements.name: a payment of a publication's tag, the ownership terms it names signed by nobody: no purchase
agreements.rule: Agreements rules 11 and 15 with rule 1: the owners' side signs only as an agreement that exists
agreements.why: Mal publishes ownership terms over Eve's film, signed by nobody, and a publication naming them, which Eve signs: no agreement exists, so the owners' side has not signed, the publication sells nothing, and the payment is owed back.

agreements.name: the same terms signed by their drafter alone: still no purchase
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 1: an agreement exists once every party signed
agreements.why: Mal signs his own draft; Eve, its other party, never does.

agreements.name: the same terms once every party signed: the agreement signs the publication, and the payment is a purchase
agreements.why: Eve signs the terms too: the agreement exists, every party of it signed the publication, and the payment of its tag naming the agreement is a purchase.

agreements.name: a purchase of the publication's tag naming its ownership agreement, its version a release of another work under another agreement: a wrong receipt
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 12: "a receipt naming a version on no line of the agreement the publication names is a wrong receipt"
agreements.why: The buyer's claim names, in field 9, the ownership agreement the publication names, and as its version a release of another work that another agreement owns. That release is on no line of the song's ownership agreement: the claim is a wrong receipt, counting for nothing.

agreements.name: the same purchase, its version the ownership agreement's founding version: a purchase
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 12: field 9 names "a version on that agreement's line"
agreements.why: The twin of the case before: the version is the ownership agreement's founding one, on a request rail.

agreements.name: a deal's complete version nothing relies on, a signer's rotation disowning its signature: the version before it in force
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 47, "What others relied on stands": a version nothing relies on yet is judged by its signatures as Identity judges them
agreements.why: Ada and Bram signed version one; Ada's rotation disowns her signature act on it, and no act names version one: it is judged by its signatures, Ada's void, so it is not complete and the founding stays in force.

agreements.name: a later complete version cloning a deal's version, then a signer's rotation disowning its signature on that version: the later version in force
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 47, "What others relied on stands": a later version cloning it (rule 45)
agreements.why: Both parties signed version two, a clone of version one; Ada then rotates, disowning her signature act on version one. Version two relies on it, so version one keeps its completeness for everyone, the disowned signature shown as a dispute, and version two, complete on a complete parent, is in force.

agreements.name: a later version cloning a deal's version, signed by its drafter alone, then a signer's rotation disowning its signature on that version: nothing relied on it, the founding in force
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 47, "What others relied on stands": a clone relies on a version only once it is itself complete
agreements.why: Ada drafts version two and signs it; Bram never does. A draft only one party signed is nobody's reliance: Ada's rotation disowns her signature on version one, which is judged by its signatures, so the founding stays in force.

agreements.name: a deal's fork settled by its judge on the request of a stake holder who is no party: it counts for nothing, the deal on its reference
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 47 ("The judge of forks acts only once activated by one of the signing parties"); settlement request (type 22): signed by a party who signed the reference; rule 35
agreements.why: Ivo holds a fifth of the song's stake and signed the founding, but is no party: his settlement request activates no judge, so the judge's settlement keeping A settles nothing.

agreements.name: the same settlement on the request of a party who signed the reference: the version kept is in force
agreements.why: Gus, a party who signed the reference, asks; the judge of forks the reference names keeps A within its period.

agreements.name: a payment under co-owners' publication every party of their ownership agreement signed, naming the agreement: a purchase
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 11 (every party signs a publication: the owners' side by every party of their agreement); rule 12
agreements.why: Hana drafts the publication of their ownership agreement, Ito signs it too; Hana, its split service, prices it by a tag, and the buyer's claim names the agreement and its version (field 9).

agreements.name: a deal one of whose parties is a deal, signed by every party of that deal's version in force: exists
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 15: a deal that is a party of another deal signs it where every party of its version in force signs it
agreements.why: The inner deal's version in force is its clone naming Jo and Lu; both sign the outer deal, and Mo signs for himself.

agreements.name: a deal one of whose parties is an agreement this verifier does not hold, every other signature held: unknown
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 15: a verifier that cannot follow every layer of it answers unknown
agreements.why: The outer deal names Nia and Oz's deal as a party; this verifier does not hold that deal's terms, so it cannot tell whose signatures sign for it, nor whether it makes a loop: not "does not exist".

agreements.name: the same at a verifier holding the inner deal: exists
agreements.why: Holding the inner deal, it follows the layer: Nia and Oz, its parties, signed the outer deal, and Pem signed for himself.

agreements.name: a free sale confirmed by the buyer's act acknowledging both the door's record of the vow and the buyer's own sign-on: confirmed
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 13: for a free sale, the buyer's act acknowledges both the act about the vow and its own signature act on the publication
agreements.why: Rafa signed the hall's publication of the free seat, which no price tag prices (the sale), then acknowledges the door's record naming the vow and that signature act.

agreements.name: a collective's grant whose acceptance an act of the collective acknowledged, after the grantee's rotation disowns it: the grantee's act is backed
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Grant (type 9)": "the grantee's acceptance is placed as a member's signature is"; "Made before, made after", 2 and 4
agreements.why: Cy, under the rule for Agreements (any one member), draws the collective's grant; the app accepts it and publishes for the collective with its own key, naming the grant; the app's rotation then disowns its acceptance. The collective's payee pointer, drawn by Cy for it, acknowledges the acceptance, or no act does.

agreements.name: the same, the acceptance acknowledged by no act of the collective: not backed
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Grant (type 9)": "the grantee's acceptance is placed as a member's signature is"; "Made before, made after", 2 and 4
agreements.why: Cy, under the rule for Agreements (any one member), draws the collective's grant; the app accepts it and publishes for the collective with its own key, naming the grant; the app's rotation then disowns its acceptance. The collective's payee pointer, drawn by Cy for it, acknowledges the acceptance, or no act does.

agreements.name: a clone marked with a succession plan alone that places the seat successor after the other parties, not in the party's place: invalid
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 83 ("A clone marked with the plan alone that changes anything more is invalid"); rule 46
agreements.why: The founding carries Ben's plan, every member signing it, his seat passing automatically to Dee. The clone takes Ben out, Dee in his place in every holding of the key grammar, and drops the plan; among the parties Dee stands last, or in Ben's place.

agreements.name: the same clone with the seat successor in the party's own place among the parties: not invalid
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 83 ("A clone marked with the plan alone that changes anything more is invalid"); rule 46
agreements.why: The founding carries Ben's plan, every member signing it, his seat passing automatically to Dee. The clone takes Ben out, Dee in his place in every holding of the key grammar, and drops the plan; among the parties Dee stands last, or in Ben's place.

agreements.name: a grantee's obligation for the collective that the collective pays on, its grant revoked by a revocation not holding it: binds
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 76 ("The grantor may adopt a void or disputed act of a grant key as its own": "pays on it"); "Made before, made after", 7
agreements.why: Cy, under the rule for Agreements, draws a grant reaching Money; the app signs an obligation of the collective to a supplier with its own key, naming the grant; Cy draws the collective's revocation of the grant, whose history does not hold the obligation. The collective's own claim, signed by Ben, whom the rule for Money names, pays the obligation (its field fulfils names it), or nothing does.

agreements.name: the same obligation the collective never paid on, acknowledged, nor cited: void
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 76 ("The grantor may adopt a void or disputed act of a grant key as its own": "pays on it"); "Made before, made after", 7
agreements.why: Cy, under the rule for Agreements, draws a grant reaching Money; the app signs an obligation of the collective to a supplier with its own key, naming the grant; Cy draws the collective's revocation of the grant, whose history does not hold the obligation. The collective's own claim, signed by Ben, whom the rule for Money names, pays the obligation (its field fulfils names it), or nothing does.

agreements.name: a member's public liveness on the collective's agreement, acknowledged by an act of the collective: shows presence
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Liveness (type 12)": "In a collective, it counts only where the collective placed it"; "Made before, made after", 2
agreements.why: Ana publishes a liveness naming the collective's founding. The collective's payee pointer, an act of its own key on its chain, acknowledges it, or no act does.

agreements.name: the same liveness no act of the collective placed: shows nothing
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Liveness (type 12)": "In a collective, it counts only where the collective placed it"; "Made before, made after", 2
agreements.why: Ana publishes a liveness naming the collective's founding. The collective's payee pointer, an act of its own key on its chain, acknowledges it, or no act does.

agreements.name: 9.1 Ana's transfer of her whole share to Cy, Cy's signature and Ana's chain signature placed: it takes effect
agreements.why: The seller signs the transfer and chain-signs it, fixing its place on her own line; the buyer completes it by his signature act. Ben is notified, not asked.

agreements.name: 9.1 the same transfer, Ana's signature alone: it does not take effect yet
agreements.why: Neither the buyer's signature act nor the seller's chain signature is placed.

agreements.name: 9.1 a purchase under the label's publication after the transfer: a purchase, neither publication changed
agreements.why: The publication reads the ownership agreement by reference: the transfer changes no publication, and the receipt names the agreement.

agreements.name: 9.1 its split, following the complete transfer, paying Cy 400,000 of every million left on the owners' line: the plan kept
agreements.why: The label takes 150 of 1,000 off the top; of the 850 left, Cy is paid 340 and Ben 510.

agreements.name: 9.1 once the transfer is complete, a split under the self-published publication paying Ana for the share: it breaks the plan
agreements.why: Both signatures are placed: the share is Cy's, so a payout of it to Ana does not match the stake.

agreements.name: 9.1 the same split, the transfer bearing only Ana's signature: it still pays Ana, the plan kept
agreements.why: The transfer is not complete: the stake is as the ownership agreement writes it.

agreements.name: 9.1 a payout receipt Ana signs for the share, bound to a rotation after her transfer's chain signature: a wrong receipt
agreements.why: Her chain signature fixed the transfer's place on her own line; a receipt she signs after it, for the stake sold, counts for nothing, and that payout is owed to Cy.

agreements.name: 9.2 a record registering Cy's resignation, drawn by Ben, naming the band and its previous decision: the line
agreements.why: Cy resigned alone; any member draws the record; it names the band as chain and the acts before it.

agreements.name: 9.2 the rotation of the band's chain key, rebuilt from Ana's and Ben's shares, declaring the clone without Cy: valid
agreements.why: Its line's history is that of the signature acts its declaration names; Ana and Ben, any two of three, meet the constitutional rule.

agreements.name: 9.2 Cy's text for the band before the line: it counts
agreements.why: Any one member may act in Text; before the line Cy is one.

agreements.name: 9.2 a pointer of the band Cy signed before the line: his signature still counts for it
agreements.rule: Agreements rules 58 and 70; "Made before, made after", 3
agreements.why: Money needs two members: Ana drafted it and Cy signed it, both members then.

agreements.name: 9.2 Cy's text naming the band after the line: it counts for nothing
agreements.why: His power ends at the line that registers his departure: the act's history holds the record.

agreements.name: 9.2 a pointer after the line, drafted by Ana and signed by Cy: it does not count
agreements.why: Money needs two members; Cy's signature after the line is no member's.

agreements.name: 9.2 the same pointer once Ben signs it too: it counts
agreements.why: Ana and Ben, two members.

agreements.name: 9.2 Cy's own post after he left: valid, untouched
agreements.why: His own key continues to sign his own acts: the post names no collective.

agreements.name: 9.2 a pointer after the line drafted by Cy, Ana and Ben both signing it: it counts for nothing
agreements.why: A member's power ends at the line that registers their departure: an act they draft for the collective after it counts for nothing, however many current members sign it.

agreements.name: 9.3 a record registering the abandonment authority's declaration of Ben: the line
agreements.why: The authority's declaration triggers the plan; any member draws the record registering it, naming the band and its genesis.

agreements.name: 9.3 the clone marked with Ben's plan, Dee in his place, every threshold unchanged, his share to his two children: not invalid
agreements.why: Marked with the plan alone, signed by the seat successor, changing only what the plan gives: Dee in Ben's seat, Ben's share of the band's stake to his two children in equal parts; Ana drafts it for the band, citing the record.

agreements.name: 9.3 the same clone changing the words too: invalid
agreements.why: A clone marked with the plan alone that changes anything more is invalid.

agreements.name: 9.3 the same clone leaving Ben's share where it was, his plan naming his children: invalid
agreements.why: A plan naming stake successors passes the party's stake to them in the clone that executes it: one leaving the stake as it was is not what the plan gives.

agreements.name: 9.3 the rotation declaring the succession clone: valid
agreements.why: The band's chain key, rebuilt, declares the clone; the keys are re-dealt to Dee in Ben's place.

agreements.name: 9.3 Dee's text for the band, citing the rotation: it counts
agreements.why: Dee holds the seat in the agreement in force for the act.

agreements.name: 9.3 a founding naming a single chain-key holder with a successor and an escrowed share: not invalid
agreements.why: A single holder still has a named successor and an escrowed share.

agreements.name: 9.3 a founding naming a single chain-key holder with neither: invalid
agreements.why: No successor is named and no share escrowed: the key would die with its holder.

agreements.name: 9.4 a fork drawn by a member, naming the band, its line and the successors, chain-signed by every member: complete
agreements.why: Each side founded its successor first; the members on each side chain-sign the fork under the constitutional change rule; there is no debt to assign.

agreements.name: 9.4 a text for the band after its fork: it counts for nothing
agreements.why: Once the fork is complete the original is closed: nothing done for it afterwards counts.

agreements.name: 9.4 a payment under the band's own publication made before the fork, which the fork's history does not hold: racing it, no purchase
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 12, "Owners that ended"; "Made before, made after", 7
agreements.why: "After it" is read as the tie rule reads an ending: the fork cites the band's last notice, not the payment, so neither cites the other, and the ending wins.

agreements.name: 9.4 a payment under the band's own publication after the fork: no purchase, owed back
agreements.why: A publication whose ownership agreement names the closed collective as owner sells nothing from the fork's line.

agreements.name: 9.4 a closing of a band that still holds half a song's stake: not complete
agreements.why: A closing ends only a collective that holds nothing: the song's ownership agreement lists the band as an owner.

agreements.name: 9.4 the band's transfer of its whole half to Dee, drawn by a member, completed by Dee, chain-signed by the band: it takes effect
agreements.why: The band is the seller: a member draws the act for it, under the rule for Agreements; its chain key fixes the transfer's place on the band's own line.

agreements.name: 9.4 the band's closing citing that transfer, chain-signed by every member: complete
agreements.why: "Holds nothing" applies the complete transfers the closing's history cites, as rule 10 counts them: the band's half is Dee's.

agreements.name: 9.5 the band's genesis, declaring its founding and no signing key, signed by a chain key revealed in its signature: valid
agreements.why: A collective's genesis is signed by a chain key revealed in its signature, its commitment naming the next.

agreements.name: 9.5 the band's rotation, signed with its chain key, receipted by its home: valid
agreements.why: It reveals the chain key the genesis committed and commits the next; it installs no signing key and keeps no tip.

agreements.name: 9.5 the band's homeless rotation, its old home objecting: it counts, its own escape endorsement
agreements.why: Signed with its chain key, rebuilt from k of its members' shares, it is its own escape endorsement; the old home's objection voids nothing.

agreements.name: 9.5 a person's homeless rotation under the same objection, with no endorsement: void
agreements.why: A person's genesis declares a signing key, so its homeless rotation is no escape endorsement of its own: a single valid objection from a live home of the old set voids it.

agreements.name: 9.6 a payment the split service received on a push rail before the ending: a purchase, past sales standing
agreements.why: On a push rail the split service settles it on its own chain: its receipt comes before its own signature on the ending.

agreements.name: 9.6 a payment the service recorded after its own signature on the version ending the publication: racing it, no purchase
agreements.why: Its receipt's history holds the service's signature on the ending: a payment racing the ending, owed back.

agreements.name: 9.6 who owes that payment back, the service having paid out the label's share and the owners' line: each party in the share it received
agreements.why: Owed back by the split service from what it holds, nothing here, and past that by each party in the share it received: the label 150, Ana 340, Ben 510.

agreements.name: 9.6 a payment following the tag's later version with no price, its signer's alone: no purchase
agreements.why: A version with no price withdraws the tag: it stops sales from then on.

agreements.name: 9.6 the sale before the withdrawal: still a purchase
agreements.why: Past sales stand.

agreements.name: 9.6 a payment naming the tag's earlier, priced version, receipted on a push rail after the withdrawal is in the service's history: no purchase
agreements.why: A sale before a tag's withdrawal is settled as a push rail settles an ending: the service's receipt comes after its own signature on the version with no price.

agreements.name: 9.7 the bake that crosses, its bytes and work hash: valid
agreements.why: A bake in core format: a MOR 2 client reads it as it is.

agreements.name: 9.7 the claim that crosses, naming who made the work: valid
agreements.why: A claim in core format.

agreements.name: 9.7 the ownership agreement that crosses, naming who owns what share: it exists
agreements.why: Every party signed it; nothing in it needs to change for a publication remade under MOR 2's rules.

agreements.name: a collective's terms naming a rule for every layer, 1 to 5: not invalid
agreements.why: Field 19 maps each layer, 1 to 5, to a rule: every party, a threshold, or named members.

agreements.name: a collective's terms naming no rule for one layer: invalid
agreements.why: Field 19 holds exactly the keys 1 to 5.

agreements.name: a collective's terms naming a rule for layer 0: invalid
agreements.why: Identity is no layer a collective acts in: key 0 is refused.

agreements.name: a collective's terms naming a rule for a layer above 5: invalid
agreements.why: There are five layers a collective acts in: a key above 5 is refused.

agreements.name: a collective's terms whose rule for a layer is counted by shares: invalid
agreements.why: A layer's rule is every party, a threshold or named members; a rule by share is the constitutional rule's form, not a layer's.

agreements.name: a collective's terms with a finer area reaching acts of one type: not invalid
agreements.why: A finer area reaches acts by [1, spec, type].

agreements.name: a collective's terms with a finer area reaching a whole layer: invalid
agreements.why: A whole layer is field 19's: an area's kinds are of the form [1, spec, type] only.

agreements.name: a record naming the collective drawn by someone who is no member: no line, nothing in force
agreements.why: Any member draws a record; one drawn by a stranger is no decision of the collective.

agreements.name: the same record drawn by Cy, a member holding nothing in particular: the clone in force
agreements.why: The clone is complete, marked by the rule for Agreements (any one member) and signed by Ana; Cy draws the record.

agreements.name: a record of a constitutional clone adding a member, the key grammar unchanged: the clone in force
agreements.why: Adding a member, no key holder leaving and the key grammar as it was, is put in force by a record.

agreements.name: a record of a clone changing the key grammar: a line, but nothing put in force
agreements.why: A clone changing the key grammar takes effect only at the rotation that declares it.

agreements.name: the rotation declaring that clone, Dee's share dealt: valid
agreements.why: The chain key, rebuilt, declares the clone with the signature acts that complete it.

agreements.name: a platform's publication of a worker's vow, no ownership agreement claiming it: a purchase, its drafter the owners' side
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 14, "A vow has an owner"; rule 11
agreements.why: A publication selling a vow no ownership agreement claims is a lone seller's: its drafter is its owners' side, and the worker, no party of it, is paid nothing by it (the stated cost).

agreements.name: a grant in an area of number one, drawn by one of the area's holders, no other signing: its grantee's act within it counts
agreements.why: The drafter's act is their signature: Ana holds the Money area, whose number is one, so the grant counts, and the agent accepted it.

agreements.name: the same grant drawn by a member holding no part of the area, no holder signing: its grantee's act counts for nothing
agreements.why: A grant never reaches beyond its issuer's power: Cy holds no part of the Money area, and neither holder signed the grant.

agreements.name: a payment to a backup the publication lists, still naming the tag, receipted by the backup in its own name: a purchase
agreements.why: Every payer tries the services in order, the payment still naming the tag; a backup receipts in its own name and splits by the same plan.

agreements.name: a succession clone putting the seat successor in the departing member's place in the rule for Text: not invalid
agreements.why: The rule for Text names Ben alone; the clone marked with his plan puts Dee in his place there, as in the key grammar, nothing else changed.

agreements.name: the same clone leaving the rule for Text naming the departed member: invalid
agreements.why: A layer's rule names parties of the agreement; Ben is no party of the clone.

agreements.name: the same clone also adding another member to the rule for Text: invalid
agreements.why: A plan's clone changes a layer's rule only by putting the seat successor in the party's place.

agreements.name: a claim a member signs for the collective, naming the collective its one creator: the collective's claim, the collective the default holder
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Claim (type 3)": its opener among its creators; rules 15, 58 and 60
agreements.why: Ben signs it with his own key, naming the collective in `objects`; any one member acts for it in Agreements. Read as rule 58 reads every act for a collective, its opener is the collective, among its creators; no other creator to sign.

agreements.name: the same: the collective the default holder of the work
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Claim (type 3)": its opener among its creators; rules 15, 58 and 60
agreements.why: One claim binds the work and no ownership agreement writes shares in it: the default holder is the claim's opener, the collective.

agreements.name: a member's claim for the collective listing that member beside it, the member's own signature act not yet given: not bound
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Claim (type 3)": its opener among its creators; rules 15, 58 and 60
agreements.why: The collective opens it; Ben, a co-creator listed beside it, is another creator, who binds it by his own signature act ("Claim (type 3)"): until then nothing binds.

agreements.name: the same, Ben's own signature act naming it: bound, the collective the default holder
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Claim (type 3)": its opener among its creators; rules 15, 58 and 60
agreements.why: Ben signs it as himself, a co-creator; the claim binds, and its opener, the collective, is the default holder.

agreements.name: a stranger's claim naming the collective its creator: nobody's claim
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Claim (type 3)": its opener among its creators; rules 15, 58 and 60
agreements.why: Anyone can write a collective's name in `objects`; a stranger's act naming it counts for nothing (rule 58), so no claim binds the work.

agreements.name: a member's claim naming the collective, the member its only creator: the collective's act, its opener not among its creators, counting for nothing
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Claim (type 3)": its opener among its creators; rules 15, 58 and 60
agreements.why: Its bytes name the collective, so it is the collective's (rule 58), and the collective is not among its creators: no claim. A member claiming for himself signs without naming the collective.

agreements.name: a claim naming neither its signer nor the collective it names among its creators: invalid
agreements.rule: Agreements, "Claim (type 3)": its opener among its creators
agreements.why: Ben signs it for the collective and lists only Ana: neither its signer nor any chain its `objects` name is among its creators, outside its format.

agreements.name: a payment naming a tag's earlier price on a push rail, the seller's receipt recorded after a later version changing the price: no purchase, owed back
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 12: a price change settled as a withdrawal is; Money rule 18
agreements.why: The seller's own history holds the version pricing the song at 1200 when it records the payment of 900 naming the earlier version: on a push rail, no purchase once the service's history holds the new version.

agreements.name: the same payment, the seller's receipt recorded before the later version: a purchase at the earlier price
agreements.rule: Agreements rule 12: a price change settled as a withdrawal is; Money rule 18
agreements.why: The receipt's history does not hold the new version: a sale at 900, past sales standing.

agreements.name: a specification naming a collective its creator, published by a member for it: the collective's
agreements.rule: Development rule 3: an act for a collective that Agreements counts, or under a grant key Agreements backs, is the creator's
agreements.why: Ana, whom the founding names for the band in Envelopes (a specification's publication is a bake), signs it naming the band in `objects`: an act for the collective that Agreements counts.

agreements.name: the same naming the collective, published by a stranger: unclaimed
agreements.rule: Development rule 3: an act for a collective that Agreements counts, or under a grant key Agreements backs, is the creator's
agreements.why: Anyone can name a collective in `objects`; a stranger's act for it counts for nothing (Agreements rule 58).

agreements.name: a specification naming a person its creator, published under her grant key that Agreements backs: hers
agreements.rule: Development rule 3: an act for a collective that Agreements counts, or under a grant key Agreements backs, is the creator's
agreements.why: Ida's grant reaches her application's bakes; the publication is signed with the grant key and cites the grant: her own act for this rule.

envelopes.name: an everyday act with two prev entries: invalid
envelopes.why: At most one entry: a sequence never branches inside one act.

envelopes.name: an act signed under a signature scheme the verifier does not implement: unknown
envelopes.why: Every rule the verifier can apply passes (shape, text, prev); only the signature cannot be checked: unknown, never valid.

envelopes.name: a text act signed under a scheme the verifier lacks, carrying acks: invalid, not unknown
envelopes.rule: Envelopes rule 30, "Invalid beats unknown"; rules 18 and 19
envelopes.why: The text's own example: a rule the verifier can apply (a text act carries no acks) fails, whatever it cannot read.

envelopes.name: an act of a specification the verifier does not implement, a map key two levels deep in its payload canonical: unknown
envelopes.why: Every rule the verifier can apply passes; its specification is one the verifier does not implement.

envelopes.name: the same with that map key not in NFC: invalid, which beats unknown
envelopes.why: Every CBOR text string in the inside, map keys included, at any depth, whatever specification the act names, is canonical text: e followed by a combining acute is not NFC.

envelopes.name: a text act carrying acks: invalid
envelopes.why: A text act MUST NOT carry acks; one that does is invalid.

envelopes.name: a reaction under a cMIP carrying acks: invalid
envelopes.rule: Envelopes rules 18 and 19; "A like is never an acknowledgement"
envelopes.why: An act whose type is not defined by Identity, Money or Agreements carrying acks is invalid, at a verifier knowing the six MIR hashes, though it implements no cMIP.

envelopes.name: a publication carrying acks: invalid
envelopes.rule: Envelopes rule 18: any other act of this MIR MUST NOT carry acks
envelopes.why: An Envelopes act carries no acks.

envelopes.name: a witness act acknowledging the same post: valid
envelopes.why: An Identity act may carry acks: the deliberate way to rely on a post.

envelopes.name: an everyday act carrying neither position nor summary: valid act by act
envelopes.rule: Envelopes rule 13: position and summary are not checked act by act, nor is their absence
envelopes.why: Judged as an act whose position or summary does not fit, which only a rebuilt line judges; prev is present, with one entry.

envelopes.name: an everyday act whose position and summary do not fit its predecessor: valid act by act
envelopes.why: Not invalid act by act; it cannot be proven kept when its line is rebuilt.

envelopes.name: a reply whose reference names a wrong signer: valid
envelopes.rule: Envelopes rule 20: an act whose reference names a wrong signer stays valid
envelopes.why: The signer beside an act id is a hint of where to look; a wrong one shows only when the reference is followed.

envelopes.name: a private routes act: invalid
envelopes.rule: Envelopes rule 8; Identity, "Every act defined by this MIR is public, except a private link"
envelopes.why: Its content key is held, as its recipient holds it; an Identity act other than a link's is public.

envelopes.name: an act of the retired type 3 naming a bake this verifier does not hold: invalid
envelopes.why: Type 3 is retired, never reused: an act of it is invalid, whatever it names.

envelopes.name: an act of the retired type 3 signed by a stranger: invalid
envelopes.why: Type 3 is retired: no authority withdraws a bake.

envelopes.name: an act of the retired type 3 signed by the identity a bake's field 8 names: invalid
envelopes.why: A bake is never withdrawn; what stops is a price tag or a publication.

envelopes.name: an act of the retired type 3 signed by the bake's uploader: invalid
envelopes.why: A bake is never withdrawn, by its uploader either: the uploader withdraws a price tag instead (Money rule 18).

envelopes.name: an act of the retired type 3 naming a text act: invalid
envelopes.why: Type 3 is retired.

envelopes.name: an act of the retired type 3 without the entry [bake, bake]: invalid
envelopes.why: Type 3 is retired.

envelopes.name: a bake carrying field 8, reserved: invalid
envelopes.why: Fields 7 and 8 are reserved, never reused: a bake names nobody it is made for.

envelopes.name: a bake carrying field 7, reserved: invalid
envelopes.why: A bake carries no price: its price is a price tag (Money type 5).

envelopes.name: a bake with fields 0 to 4 and nothing reserved: valid
envelopes.why: A bake says only who uploaded it.

envelopes.name: an Envelopes act of type 2, retired: invalid
envelopes.rule: Envelopes rule 30; "Types defined by this MIR": type 2 retired, never reused
envelopes.why: An act of a type this MIR does not define is invalid.

envelopes.name: a bake without its nonce (field 4): invalid
envelopes.why: A payload outside its type's format is invalid.

envelopes.name: a key delivery whose key does not open the act it names: valid as an act
envelopes.rule: Envelopes rule 11: valid as an act by its shape; its key used only if it opens what it names
envelopes.why: Its key is ignored and shown so; the act itself stands.

envelopes.name: a key delivery carrying no key: invalid
envelopes.why: Field 1, the key, is required.

envelopes.name: an X-Wing encryption key of 1216 bytes, version 1: valid
envelopes.why: Scheme 4, a 1216-byte key, version 1 naming nothing it replaces.

envelopes.name: an X-Wing encryption key of 1215 bytes: invalid
envelopes.why: An X-Wing key of another length than 1216 bytes makes the act invalid.

envelopes.name: an encryption key under scheme 1, a signature scheme: invalid
envelopes.rule: Envelopes, "Encryption key (type 4)": numbers 1 to 3 are signature schemes and are never encryption keys
envelopes.why: enc-key's scheme is 4 or a specification hash.

envelopes.name: an X-Wing encryption key of 1216 bytes, private: invalid
envelopes.rule: Envelopes rule 8: Identity acts and this MIR's encryption keys are public acts, save a private link
envelopes.why: A well-formed key, sealed to one reader: an encryption key must be public, so which key is current is the same for every verifier.

identity.name: a genesis, valid
identity.why: Signed by the signing key it declares, with a home.

identity.name: a genesis signed by a key it does not declare
identity.why: A genesis MUST be signed by the signing key it declares.

identity.name: a rotation counting on its home's receipt
identity.rule: Identity, "Which rotation counts"; receipt checks 1 to 6
identity.why: The home the rule names receipted it.

identity.name: a rotation not yet receipted: pending
identity.why: No receipt of its home yet.

identity.name: an act bound to a pending rotation: pending
identity.why: Its binding is a rotation that does not count yet.

identity.name: two genuine rotations receipted by one home: contested
identity.why: Neither receipt counts; the identity is contested at position 1, not frozen.

identity.name: an act a rotation disowns: void
identity.why: Disowned, relied on by nobody.

identity.name: a disowned act another identity acknowledged: disputed
identity.why: Another identity acknowledged it by a witness act (Identity type 15).

identity.name: a disowned act its deal's keeper recorded before the rotation: disputed
identity.rule: Identity rule 34; Agreements rules 41 and 42, "Belongs to", "Keeper record (type 2)"
identity.why: The act names the deal in objects, so belongs to it; the keeper the deal names recorded it before recording the rotation. The keeper records are type 2 acts the verifier reads; Agreements tells Identity which acts its keepers rescue.

identity.name: the same recorded by a keeper the deal does not name: void
identity.why: A record counts only from a keeper named by an agreement the act belongs to.

identity.name: an escape: a homeless rotation endorsed by the signing key
identity.why: Both keys, its new home's receipt; no old home's receipt is needed.

identity.name: a rotation declaring a successor: it counts, the succession declared
identity.why: The rotation counts; the successor is shown as declared until it confirms.

identity.name: the succession, unconfirmed: declared, not followed
identity.why: The successor has not confirmed it.

identity.name: the succession confirmed by the successor's link confirmation naming the rotation: followed
identity.why: A succession to a MOR identity is followed once that identity confirms it.

identity.name: a receipt from an operator that is no home of the identity changes nothing
identity.why: Only the homes the rule names count.

identity.name: a home receipting two genuine rotations at one position, both under cosigned summaries: proven dishonest there
identity.why: The identity requires audit; both receipts sit under cosigned log summaries, and a cosigned receipt survives the home's rotation. Position 2 counts on homes 2 and 3; home 1 counts for nothing for this identity after position 2.

identity.name: two rotations at one position, both passing the checks, the home rule deciding for the other: not counting
identity.rule: Identity, "Which rotation counts", a rotation that does not count; rules 40 and 41
identity.why: Two of three homes receipted the other; this one passes the rotation checks and loses: neither invalid nor void.

identity.name: an act bound to the rotation that does not count: invalid
identity.rule: Identity, "Which rotation counts", a rotation that does not count; everyday check 2
identity.why: Its binding names no act that counts.

identity.name: an act bound to a contested rotation: pending
identity.why: One home receipted two rotations at position 1: the position is contested, and an act bound to either waits until the contest ends.

identity.name: a kept tip whose summary does not fit its line, the line held: the tip keeps nothing, itself void
identity.why: The rotation names two tips; one's summary is not the summary of its line up to it, which the verifier holds.

identity.name: an act below that tip: void
identity.why: The rotation names two tips; one's summary is not the summary of its line up to it, which the verifier holds.

identity.name: an act on the rotation's other tip, which fits: valid
identity.why: The rotation names two tips; one's summary is not the summary of its line up to it, which the verifier holds.

identity.name: a rotation whose one kept tip does not fit its line, the line held: it stands, valid
identity.why: A tip that does not fit never makes the rotation invalid: its validity is fixed by its bytes.

identity.name: its tip, which does not fit: void, kept by nothing
identity.why: The tip keeps nothing, itself included.

identity.name: a disowned act acknowledged only by an act signed with another identity's scoped key: void
identity.why: An acknowledgement counts only under the acknowledging identity's signing key, never a scoped key: reliance is the identity's, not a grantee's.

identity.name: a private link claim, its key held, found at no home of its signer: unknown
identity.why: A private link counts only once found at a home its signer's chain names; found nowhere, unknown, never invalid.

identity.name: the same found at its signer's own home: valid
identity.why: Ana's genesis names herself as her home; the claim was found there.

identity.name: a private link claim found at the home its signer's chain named at its binding, the signer having moved homes since: valid
identity.why: The claim is bound to Ana's genesis, which names the first home; a later rotation keeping it moves her to another home. A later move of homes does not void a link found where the chain named its homes at the binding.

identity.name: the same found only at the home the signer moved to: unknown
identity.why: The homes that count are those the chain names at the link act's binding, not the latest: found only at the new home, the claim is not yet found where it counts, so unknown, never invalid.

identity.name: two homeless rotations at one position, each final, with an objection whose status cannot be told there: contested
identity.rule: Identity, "What stops a chain", the order of the reasons; "Final"; the homeless procedure
identity.why: Each homeless rotation is an escape receipted by its new home, and each is followed by a rotation counting under the rule it declared: both are final. A contest among final rotations comes before cannot tell, since no objection can undo it; the old home's objection, bound to a rotation not held, cannot be told.

identity.name: an escape, final, and an ordinary rotation its old home receipts at the same position: the ordinary rotation counts
identity.rule: Identity, "The homeless procedure": a rotation counting under the home rule always beats a homeless one
identity.why: Eda escaped to a new home and rotated again there; her old home, still alive, receipts an ordinary rotation at position 1. The rotation counting under the rule in force wins; the escape and what follows it count for nothing.

identity.name: the escape in that case: not counting
identity.rule: Identity, "The homeless procedure"; "Which rotation counts", a rotation that does not count
identity.why: It passes its checks and loses at its position.

identity.name: an escape, endorsed with the signing key, against its old home's valid objection: it counts
identity.rule: Identity, "The homeless procedure", the escape: both keys need no old home
identity.why: The old home objects to the homeless rotation; an escape signed by both keys and receipted by its new home needs no old home's word, and an objection does not undo it.

identity.name: a self-hosted identity's rotation: it counts, no receipt needed
identity.rule: Identity, homes: a self-hosted identity is its own home
identity.why: Sol's genesis names itself as its home; the rotation it signs is served by itself.

identity.name: a self-hosted identity serving two rotations at one position: contested
identity.why: Two rotations at position 1, both served by the identity itself.

identity.name: a rotation built on a rotation not yet receipted: pending
identity.why: The first rotation waits on its home's receipt; the second, on the first, does not count yet either, and may once the receipts arrive: never invalid.

identity.name: an act bound to that second rotation: pending
identity.why: Signed with the key the second rotation installs; its binding does not count yet.

identity.name: the same once the home has receipted both rotations: the act valid
identity.why: Both rotations now count; the act bound to the second is valid.

identity.name: a rotation built on a rotation that does not count: invalid
identity.rule: Identity, "Which rotation counts", a rotation that does not count; everyday check 2
identity.why: The rotation it builds on lost its position for good; nothing it waits on can make it count.

identity.name: a homeless rotation, its old homes gone by closure but one, followed by an escape through other homes: the living old home's objection still voids it
identity.rule: Identity, "Finality": final once a rotation at n plus one counts under the home rule the homeless rotation declared
identity.why: Two of Oda's three homes closed, so her homeless rotation to a new home counts, provisionally. The next rotation is an escape that counts through a home of its own, not through the new home's receipt: it does not make the first final, and the third home's objection voids it, and the escape built on it.

identity.name: the same, followed by a rotation its new home receipts: final, the late objection voids nothing
identity.why: The next rotation counts under the home rule the homeless rotation declared: the homeless rotation is final, and the objection that surfaces after it changes nothing.

identity.name: the same escape, its new home's receipt held: it counts
identity.why: Both keys, and the new home's receipt: the way out of a position contested at a self-hosted home.

identity.name: a disowned act whose only acknowledgement is by an identity whose genesis is not held: unknown
identity.rule: Identity, section 6: a verifier that cannot tell answers unknown, never valid, void or invalid; disputed waits on void as well
identity.why: Whether the acknowledgement counts cannot be told, so neither can whether the act is relied on: unknown, not void.

identity.name: the same with the acknowledger's genesis held: disputed
identity.why: The acknowledgement is valid: the act is relied on.

identity.name: a rotation installing a Schnorr signing key of 31 bytes: invalid
identity.rule: Identity, "Encoding and conventions": a key of a founding scheme whose length is not the one in the table makes the act invalid
identity.why: Scheme 1 keys are 32 bytes; its home's receipt changes nothing.

identity.name: a rotation installing a 31-byte key of a scheme named by hash: valid
identity.rule: Identity, "Encoding and conventions": a scheme named by hash, whatever the lengths
identity.why: Lengths are checked only for founding schemes; a rotation's validity never depends on the kind of signing key it installs.

identity.name: a rotation whose only receipt its home's rotation voided, the receipt acknowledged: pending, not contested
identity.rule: Identity, receipt check 6: it blocks nothing; "Definitions": a contested position comes from rules 40, 44 and 4
identity.why: The voided receipt is a visible dispute and never support; no conflict under rules 40, 44 or 4 stands: the rotation waits on a receipt.

identity.name: two rotations at one position, each receipted by one of three homes under a threshold of two: contested
identity.rule: Identity rule 40: if none meets the rule, the identity is contested until one does
identity.why: The homes disagree and neither rotation meets the rule.

identity.name: the same with only one home's receipt held: pending
identity.why: No home disagrees: the rotation waits on a second home's receipt.

identity.name: a succession to a "mor" identifier of 31 bytes: no succession
identity.rule: Identity, Part three, `successor`: a "mor" identifier of another length names no MOR identity, and no client follows it
identity.why: Not another protocol's succession, which a cMIP could follow: it names nothing.

identity.name: a succession to another protocol: that protocol's
identity.rule: Identity, "Succession": confirmed as that protocol's link cMIP says
identity.why: Another protocol's identifier, whatever its length.

identity.name: an escape endorsement bound to an older rotation that set the same key: no escape
identity.rule: Identity, "The escape endorsement": its binding names the act just before the homeless rotation
identity.why: The second rotation re-installed the first's key; the endorsement names the first. It is no escape endorsement, and the old home is not gone: the homeless rotation does not count.

identity.name: the same endorsement bound to the act just before: an escape, it counts
identity.why: Bound to the rotation just before the homeless one.

identity.name: a collective's genesis, declaring its founding agreement and no signing key, signed by the chain key its signature reveals: valid
identity.why: A genesis without a signing key is a collective's: it declares its founding agreement, and is signed by a chain key revealed in its signature, field 1 committing the next.

identity.name: a genesis with no signing key that declares no founding agreement: invalid
identity.why: Only a collective's genesis goes without a signing key, and it must declare its founding agreement.

identity.name: a collective's rotation installing a signing key: invalid
identity.why: An identity whose genesis declares no signing key never has one: its rotations install none and keep no tip.

identity.name: the same collective's rotation installing none: valid
identity.why: Signed with the chain key the genesis committed, revealing it and committing the next.

identity.name: an everyday act signed as the collective itself, bound to its genesis: invalid
identity.why: A collective has no signing key: it acts only through acts its members and grantees sign with their own keys, naming it.

identity.name: a specification published by the creator it names: claimed
identity.why: Ida's publication carries content naming Ida as creator.

identity.name: the same specification published by another identity: unclaimed by the creator it names
identity.why: Kit publishes Ida's content; only a publication signed by the creator named inside claims it.

identity.name: a publication the creator's rotation disowned: unclaimed
identity.why: Signed with Ida's stolen key; Ida's rotation disowns it and nobody relied on it.

identity.name: a disowned publication another identity relied on: unclaimed, shown as disputed
identity.rule: Development rule 3: a special case beside Identity rule 34
identity.why: A reader acknowledged it before the rotation: shown as disputed, and it claims nothing for the creator.

identity.name: a rotation to a signing key of a scheme named by hash, which this client has not adopted: valid
identity.rule: Development, "A signature scheme (kind 5)"; freeze scenario, Part two
identity.why: The rotation is signed under the old key; it installs a key of a scheme the client does not implement.

identity.name: a later act signed under that scheme: unknown, never valid or invalid
identity.why: A client that has not adopted the scheme answers unknown for every act signed under it, whatever the lengths.

identity.name: a self-hosted identity's homeless rotation, receipted by its new home, no escape endorsement: pending
identity.rule: Identity rule 4; the homeless procedure, step 4 (a self-hosted home is never gone); section 11
identity.why: Its old home is the identity itself, never gone: step 4 is never met, so the rotation does not count without an escape endorsement, and waits for one.

identity.name: the same: an act bound to it, pending
identity.rule: Identity rule 4; the homeless procedure, step 4 (a self-hosted home is never gone); section 11
identity.why: Everyday check 2: bound to a rotation that does not count yet.

identity.name: the same rotation with the owner's escape endorsement: it counts, once the new home's receipt meets its rule
identity.rule: Identity rule 4; section 11, "The escape endorsement"; step 5
identity.why: The owner's escape endorsement, signed with the key bound before it, skips steps 3 and 4; the new home's receipt meets the home rule the rotation declares.

identity.name: a homeless rotation a live old home's valid objection names: void
identity.rule: Identity, "Which rotation counts": a valid objection voids a homeless rotation, and with it every rotation built on it
identity.why: Steps 2 and 3 keep applying until it is final; the old home's objection, valid, voids it.

identity.name: the rotation built on it: void with it, never invalid
identity.rule: Identity, "Which rotation counts": a valid objection voids a homeless rotation, and with it every rotation built on it
identity.why: It fails no rule of its own: it is voided with the rotation it is built on.

identity.name: an act bound to the rotation built on it: invalid
identity.why: Bound to a rotation that does not count.
